chunks: And what Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Abū Isḥāq, from Nūḥ ibn Shuʿayb al-Khurāsānī, from Bashīr, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A well into which a drop of blood or wine has dripped. He said: Blood, wine, carrion, and pig meat are all one in that regard: twenty buckets are to be drawn from it; and if the odor prevails, it should be drained until it becomes wholesome.

So these two reports are not acted upon, because they are solitary reports, and the reports that we have presented earlier are not opposed by them. Also because impurity is known by the occurrence of wine in it, and we do not know with certainty its purification except by drawing out all the water of the well, so practice should accordingly be based on that. It is also possible that the report is specific to the ruling of urine, because the urine of a man necessitates drawing forty buckets, as we explained in Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām; and likewise is the ruling of blood, carrion, and pig meat. Thus, the addition of wine to that may be an error from the narrator.

key_terms.أَخْبَارِ آحَادٍ: solitary reports not sufficient here to override stronger narrations
key_terms.النَّجَاسَةَ: ritual impurity established in the water
key_terms.بِئْرٌ: a well used as a water source
key_terms.خَمْرٍ: wine, treated here as a source of najasah
key_terms.طَهَارَتَهَا: the purification of the well water
key_terms.قَطْرَةُ دَمٍ: a drop of blood falling into the well
key_terms.وَهْمًا: an error or mistaken addition by the narrator
key_terms.يُنْزَحُ: water is drawn out or removed from the well

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling in al-Istibṣār on a well contaminated by blood or wine?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling of a well into which blood or wine falls, stating that a set number of buckets should be drawn out, with further draining if the odor remains. The accompanying juristic note explains that this report is not relied upon in practice, because stronger reports indicate that certainty of purification in the case of wine requires draining all the water of the well.
